types.description: ET 200S TM-E15C24-01 spring-terminal base; partial functional interface model

document.title: SIMATIC ET 200S distributed I/O - Terminal modules
document.pages: 7, 21-22; named P1/P2 rails additionally verified in system manual 07/2003, printed 3-22 / PDF 68

modelingNotes: One physical TM-E15C24-01 base per instance; Siemens order 6ES7193-4CB30-0AA0 is packaged as five units. The inserted electronic module and optional shield-contact element are separate components.

1 through 8 are manufacturer field-clamp markings, arranged as paired front-view rows 1/5, 2/6, 3/7, 4/8. EM.n names the base-side electronic-module interface of that individual conductor, not a verified connector cavity number. The inserted electronic module determines field signal assignments.

P1 and P2 are the manufacturer power-bus names shown for this exact named variant in system-manual table 3-8, printed 3-22 / PDF 68. L/R are library aliases for inter-base ends and EM is the separate tap to the electronic-module interface. Each bus passes through this terminal base; P1 and P2 remain distinct. These aliases specify neither physical connector coordinates nor operating polarity.

AUX1.L/R are library aliases for the independent auxiliary through-bus ends. No AUX1 field clamp, field-to-AUX1 connection or AUX1-to-EM tap is shown for TM-E15C24-01. Do not import terminals A3/A4/A7/A8 or links to field terminals 4/8 from an AUX-access variant.

Backplane contacts are not pin-enumerated in the reviewed drawings. The depicted backplane is an aggregate communication/electronics-supply bus, not a single physical conductor. No backplane pin, opaque-bus short circuit or backplane fixed link is invented.

System manual section 10.8, printed 10-22 / PDF 272, documents a spring contact for noise diversion from the electronic module to the DIN rail; figure 5-1, printed 5-6 / PDF 110, identifies it as functional ground (FG). This FG mating/rail interface is omitted from the authored endpoints because its exact connector contacts are not established. It is not AUX1, and no FG-to-AUX1 or FG-to-P2 bond is asserted. Connection coverage remains partial.

All conformance fixed links require explicit project jumpers. Eight field-to-EM links, two separate tapped power-bus groups and one AUX1 through-link are represented. Single-terminal functions and connector metadata do not join nets; no continuity through the installed electronic module is asserted.

AUX1 capability up to 230 VAC or protective-conductor-bar use is described on terminal-manual page 7. Its installed potential is application-dependent. P1/P2 receive the associated power-module supply. No nominal_voltage, unconditional 24 V/M assignment, PE bond or scalar current rating is inferred. Separate drawn paths do not establish safety isolation; system-manual printed 3-6 cautions about AUX1 versus P1/P2 when different potentials are applied.

15 x 132 x 43 mm, approximately 65 g. No universally required external field connection is established for this passive base; usage and permitted potential depend on the selected electronics. Installed revision, compatibility, conductor capacity and loading need the appropriate component/application documentation.

connectionCoverage.notes: Eight field-clamp paths and their electronic-module interfaces, separate P1/P2 buses with EM taps, and the independent AUX1 through-bus are represented with qualified library aliases. Backplane pin count/functions/continuity and the documented FG spring-contact mating/rail interface are not modeled. No physical connector pin inventory, electronic-module function, shield accessory or installed bonding is claimed complete.
